clue.text: Servant's goodbye coming with retirement finally

parts.note: vale is Latin for farewell, used in English as a goodbye

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word retirement

explanation.surface: A servant says farewell as their retirement at last arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes the T at the end of 'retirement'; the 's after Servant is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A valet is a manservant who looks after his employer's clothes and personal needs.

clue.text: Devious devil, one sort of agent briefly turning to wit

indicators.note: devious means winding or crooked, so the word devil is twisted round

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: turning means the short detective word is read backwards

parts.note: tec is short for detective, a sort of agent

explanation.surface: A cunning devil and a secret agent turn to humour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Devious' rearranges DEVIL into VIDEL; 'turning' reverses TEC into CET. 'wit' looks like humour but 'to wit' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Videlicet, abbreviated viz., is Latin for namely, which is what to wit means.

clue.text: Wants to be sluggish, first to last

indicators.note: first to last says the opening letter moves to the end of the word

parts.note: to slack is to be sluggish or idle

explanation.surface: Someone longs to laze about, a race from first to last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first to last' moves the S of SLACK to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacks means is without, which is the old sense of wants, as in 'wants for nothing'.

clue.text: Tree in delta below river

indicators.note: below says the remaining pieces come under the river in this down answer

parts.note: the Tamar is a river forming the Devon and Cornwall border in England
D is delta in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A tree grows in a river delta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delta' looks like the mouth of a river, but it is the letter D. The Tamar is the river between Devon and Cornwall in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The tamarind is a tropical tree whose pods give a sour pulp used in cooking.

clue.text: Poet taking time around end of autumn to find wild animal's domain

parts.note: Homer is the ancient Greek epic poet

indicators.note: around tells us the time word wraps round the next piece

parts.note: an age is a period of time

indicators.note: end of picks the closing letter of the word autumn

explanation.surface: A poet spends an autumn hour seeking out where wild creatures live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' wraps the time word round N, the last letter of 'autumn'; 'taking' and 'to find' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A home range is the area an animal habitually lives and forages in, a zoological term.

clue.text: Hotel dealt with trouble, bringing acclaim

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A hotel handled a complaint well and was praised.
explanation.definitionFit: To hail is to greet with praise, as in a player hailed as a hero, so it means acclaim.

clue.text: Get men into reorganising plant

indicators.note: reorganising means arranging differently, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A manager brings new staff into a factory being restructured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks like a factory, but it is the definition: a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Mignonette is a fragrant garden plant of the genus Reseda.

clue.text: A politician in socialist hue rushed around violently

indicators.note: in says the A-and-politician pair goes inside the colour word

parts.note: red is the colour associated with socialism
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A left-wing MP charged about wildly.
explanation.definitionFit: To ramp is to rush about wildly or rage, so ramped is rushed around violently.

clue.text: Drinks late on? They won't help you keep a cool head then

definitions.text: They won't help you keep a cool head then
definitions.meaning: ... are knitted hats worn in bed, so they keep the head warm, not cool

explanation.surface: Late drinks won't help you stay calm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keep a cool head' reads as staying calm; literally a cap worn at night keeps your head warm.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightcap is both a bedtime drink and a cap worn in bed.

clue.text: Wholehearted bore needing an audience

indicators.note: needing an audience says the word is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: an eagre is a tidal bore, a wave surging up a river

explanation.surface: A tedious person keen to have listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bore' looks like a dull person, but it is a tidal wave up an estuary, an eagre, said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Eager means keen and enthusiastic, putting your whole heart into something.

clue.text: Leaving the City area — it's stifling outside

indicators.note: outside says the stifling word sits around the City piece

parts.note: damping, as in damping down a fire, means stifling or suppressing
EC is the postcode area of the City of London

explanation.surface: Someone is quitting the City because the air outside is oppressive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's stifling outside' reads as the weather, but 'outside' is the container signal. The City is London's financial district, whose postcode area is EC.
explanation.definitionFit: Decamping means departing suddenly, so it fits leaving as a synonym.

clue.text: London giant's journey featured in periodical

indicators.note: featured in says the journey word appears inside the periodical word

parts.note: mag is short for magazine, a periodical
a go can mean a trip or journey, as in a go on the train

explanation.surface: A magazine runs an article on the travels of a London giant.
explanation.walkthrough: Gog and Magog are the legendary giants whose effigies guard London's Guildhall and parade in the Lord Mayor's Show.
explanation.definitionFit: Magog is one of the two traditional guardian giants of the City of London.

clue.text: Something attractive about holy person?

indicators.note: about says the attractive word goes round the holy person

parts.note: a lure is something that attracts, like bait
ST is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A question about what makes a saint appealing.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: the glow or halo round a saint is a kind of lustre, an attractive sheen.
explanation.definitionFit: Lustre is a gentle shine or glory, the radiance pictured round a saint and an attractive quality.

clue.text: It's all right to interrupt one funny person or another

indicators.note: to interrupt says the all-right word breaks into the funny-person word

parts.note: a jester is a court clown, one kind of funny person
OK means all right

explanation.surface: Someone politely allows a comedian to be cut off by another.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the clue: JESTER is one funny person, and the answer is 'another' funny person, a joker.
explanation.definitionFit: A jokester is a person given to joking, so it is another sort of comic beside the jester.

clue.text: Said annual travelling around should be in part of Spain

indicators.note: travelling around means moving about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone says a yearly tour should take in a Spanish region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'should be' is a link; the definition describes the answer as an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Andalusian means of or located in Andalusia, a region of southern Spain.

clue.text: Religiously committed school entertaining archdeacon with a set of holy books

indicators.note: entertaining means holding as a guest, so the school word holds the rest inside

parts.note: a coed is a coeducational school
Ven, short for Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon
NT is the New Testament, a set of holy books

explanation.surface: A devout school hosts a senior cleric bearing scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertaining' means holding the cleric, the A and the books inside the school. An archdeacon in the Church of England is styled 'the Venerable'.
explanation.definitionFit: Covenanted means bound by a solemn religious covenant, as the Scottish Covenanters were.

clue.text: Savage — time to oust one, right?

indicators.note: to oust means to push out, so the time word replaces the one

parts.note: vicious means savage or fierce
I is the Roman numeral for one
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A question of whether something savage is justified once time has passed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to oust' replaces the first I of VICIOUS with ERA.
explanation.definitionFit: Veracious means truthful, and a right answer or account is a true one.

clue.text: Good wood is cut

parts.note: ash is a timber from the ash tree

explanation.surface: Good timber has been cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A gash is a deep cut or slash, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Food in France perhaps a mother's cooked, full of energy

indicators.note: full of says the rearranged letters hold the energy letter
cooked means doctored or altered, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written without the apostrophe
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A mother prepares a hearty meal in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges A MOTHERS, and 'full of' puts E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Horse meat is eaten in France, so it is food there, which the 'perhaps' acknowledges.

clue.text: Plain folk from the south irked, note, with everyone

indicators.note: from the south means reading up the down light, so the pieces run backwards

parts.note: sore means annoyed or irked
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Simple people from down south are annoyed with everybody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain folk' looks like ordinary people, but means people of the plains. 'from the south' reverses SORENALL.
explanation.definitionFit: Llaneros are the cowboys and herders of the llanos, the grassy plains of Venezuela and Colombia.

clue.text: Session spanning winter months

indicators.note: spanning means stretching across, so the answer sits across the two words

explanation.surface: A session that runs through the cold months of the year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spanning' takes the letters across the join of 'winTER Months'.
explanation.definitionFit: A term is a session of a school, university or court, a fixed period of sitting.

clue.text: Running late, trains can pose a problem?

indicators.note: running here means operating in a different order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Delayed trains are a nuisance for commuters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running late' looks like a train timetable phrase; 'Running' is the anagram signal on LATE TRAINS, and 'can pose' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tantaliser is a teasing puzzle or brainteaser, which is a kind of problem.

clue.text: Is daughter given order to follow women's good sense?

indicators.note: to follow says the next pieces come after the women letter

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for women
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A daughter honoured after other women: is this good sense?
explanation.walkthrough: The Order of Merit (OM) is an exclusive British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Wisdom is sound judgement, the quality of having good sense.

clue.text: Female performance promises to be divisive

parts.note: an act is a performance on stage
IOUs are written promises to pay

explanation.surface: A woman's show of promises is set to split opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: Factious means given to faction and dissension, so it causes division.

clue.text: Garbage left abandoned staff finally collected in interval

indicators.note: collected means taken in, so the shortened word holds the final letter
abandoned means given up, so the left letter is dropped

parts.note: filth means dirt or garbage

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the word staff

explanation.surface: Rubbish left behind is gathered up by staff during a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' drops L from FILTH to give FITH, which 'collected' wraps round F. 'interval' looks like a break but is the musical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A fifth is a musical interval spanning five notes of the scale.

clue.text: What's crazy in a French female — and maybe divine?

indicators.note: in says the crazy word sits inside the French word

parts.note: une is the French feminine word for a or one
mad means crazy

explanation.surface: A question about a mad Frenchwoman who might be a goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divine' is the noun, a god: theologians call God unmade, uncreated, hence 'maybe'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something divine may be thought of as uncreated, never made by anyone, hence unmade.

clue.text: Residence of a German man of law

parts.note: Johann Bode was the German astronomer of the Titius-Bode law of planetary distances

explanation.surface: The home of a German lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man of law' suggests a lawyer, but it is a scientist with a law named after him.
explanation.definitionFit: An abode is a dwelling place or home, a residence.

clue.text: Maybe lost dog has run away for stick

indicators.note: away says the run letter is taken out

parts.note: a stray is an animal with no home, perhaps a lost dog
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A lost dog has bolted for a stick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has run away' drops R from STRAY; 'stick' looks like a dog's toy but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay means to remain, to stick in a place, as in stick around.

clue.text: Fare to get across lake or swamp

indicators.note: to get across means to span, so the food word reaches over the lake letter

parts.note: fare means food, as in hearty fare

explanation.surface: Travellers pay a fare to cross a lake or marsh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fare' looks like a ticket price, but it is food.
explanation.definitionFit: To flood means to swamp, to overwhelm with water; both are verbs here.

clue.text: Barge in season, heading off south east, beyond river

indicators.note: beyond says the south-east piece comes after the river
heading off means the season word loses its first letter

parts.note: winter is a season
the Po is Italy's longest river

explanation.surface: A barge travels south-east past a river in season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barge' looks like a boat, but 'Barge in' is the definition. 'heading off' drops W from WINTER to give INTER.
explanation.definitionFit: To interpose is to intervene or interrupt, which is what barging in does.

clue.text: Spooner's sentimentality, something sweet providing inducement

indicators.note: Spooner's tells us to swap the opening sounds of the two words, after Revd Spooner

parts.note: mush is soppy sentimentality
honey is something sweet

explanation.surface: Sweet sentimentality offered as a bribe.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the first letters of MUSH HONEY gives HUSH MONEY.
explanation.definitionFit: Hush money is a payment made to buy someone's silence, a bribe or inducement.

clue.text: Exhausted author lying in street

indicators.note: lying in says the author word lies inside the street word

parts.note: a pen is used to author things, a writer

explanation.surface: A worn-out writer is sprawled in the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Spent means used up, tired out, a synonym of exhausted.
